input: Research Boeing (boeing.com) for a hedge fund

risks.claim: 737 ramp execution risk: stabilization at 47 planes/month slipped into early 2027 and the step-up to 52/month to back half of 2027 — the core driver of the cut delivery guidance and the pushed-out $10B FCF target (now 2029)

Commercial Airplanes lost $697M in Q3 2026 (margin -6.5%) on the decision to delay 737/787 rate increases and higher estimated supply chain costs; TTM operating margin ex-gain is only 0.2% and shareholders' equity is just $6.5B

Fixed-price defense contract charge cycle continues: T-7A reach-forward loss of $1.77B (2024), KC-46A losses of $0.6B (Q4 2025), VC-25B losses of $280M (Q2 2026); potential new charges remain on VC-25B, T-7A, MQ-25 and Starliner

Spirit integration costs are still growing: inherited customer deals now estimated at $1.52B (+$455M, ~43% above the initial estimate), with Boeing saying its assessment is preliminary and customers/programs unidentified

777X certification has slipped at least into 2027, with GE Aerospace still resolving a GE9X mid-seal durability issue needed for ETOPS authorization — a repeat-delay risk on the biggest widebody program

Litigation tail: in May 2026 a jury ordered Boeing to pay $49.5M to the family of a 737 MAX crash victim (Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302); FAA certification of the MAX 10 still requires each aircraft to be shown built to approved design

The just-announced 5% commercial workforce cut (notified December 2026) risks production friction during the ramp, and comes on top of the 2024 ~17,000-person reduction; SPEEA meets management the week of Nov 9 on how cuts affect members

catalysts.claim: Boeing reports Q4/FY2026 results on Jan 27, 2027; current consensus EPS -$0.708 on revenue of $25.62B

FAA certified the 737-10 (largest 737 MAX variant) on Oct 20, 2026, clearing the way for deliveries 'in the coming months'; Boeing expects first MAX 10 deliveries in 2027; ~45 MAX 7/-10 aircraft sit in inventory ready to deliver
737 production stabilization at 47/month moved into early 2027 with a step-up to 52/month in back half of 2027; next 787 rate increase planned from Dec 2026
777-9 (777X) first delivery on track for 2027, with certification flight testing progressing; certification activity continues into 2027

Boeing selected by the U.S. Navy to design, build and deliver the F/A-XX next-generation fighter; award not yet in backlog pending a source selection review — confirmation would add a major defense program

6.00% Series A mandatory convertible preferred stock ($5.75B liquidation preference) mandatorily converts into common stock on Oct 15, 2027 — a known equity-supply event just beyond the 6-month window

event_driven.claim: Boeing completed its all-stock acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems on Dec 8, 2025 (equity value $4.7B, enterprise value about $8.3B), absorbing ~15,000 employees and its largest supplier's 737 fuselage and 767/777/787 structures work; regulators required divestiture of Airbus-related sites to Airbus
Spirit takeover costs keep rising: Boeing now estimates inherited Spirit customer deals will cost $1.52B, $455M (~43%) above its end-of-2025 estimate, with the assessment still preliminary
Digital Aviation Solutions (Jeppesen, ForeFlight) sold to Thoma Bravo for $10.55B on Oct 31, 2025, generating a $9.57B gain in Q4 2025 — the portfolio move that funded deleveraging
No common dividend since 2020 and no buybacks; capital returns limited to the 6.00% mandatory convertible preferred issued Oct 2024

output.research_view: The stock now trades on execution: stabilization at 47 737s/month slipped into early 2027, 2026 737 deliveries were guided below 500, and the $10B FCF goal moved to 2029, so the next six months hinge on converting the newly certified 737-10 (first deliveries 2027) and holding the ~$2B 2026 FCF guide into the Jan 27, 2027 print. The credit story is improving faster than the P&L — debt is down $8.2B in 2026 to $45.9B against $20.7B cash, and Fitch moved to BBB-/Positive in June 2026 — but Commercial Airplanes' -6.5% margin, ongoing fixed-price defense charges, and rising Spirit integration costs keep underlying earnings near zero. Director buying (~$1.5M by Mollenkopf and Buckley) right after the 10.75% earnings-day drop and a record $745B backlog make this a show-me long into delivery/FCF execution, with the workforce cut and 777X timing the main near-term swing risks.

credit_signals.claim: At Sep 30, 2026: cash and marketable securities $20.7B, consolidated debt $45.9B (down $8.2B from FY2025's $54.1B; net debt $25.2B); debt repayments of $8,415M in the first nine months of 2026
$10.0B of credit facilities fully undrawn; short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt $4,569M at quarter end
Fitch affirmed Boeing's Long-Term IDR at BBB- and revised the outlook to Positive on Jun 26, 2026; USCP program rated F3 ($9.47B)

Ratings stand at BBB- (Fitch) / Baa3 (Moody's) — low investment grade; Moody's downgraded to Baa3 with negative outlook in April 2024 and flagged $8.0B of 2026 maturities, since refinanced/deleveraged
Nearest identified bond maturity: $300M of 2.8% notes due Mar 1, 2027 (CUSIP 097023BU8), within roughly five months of today
DOJ settlement payments of approximately $0.7B weighed on Q3 2026 operating cash flow — a non-operating cash call alongside the deleveraging

missing_fields: Exact FY2026 consensus detail beyond the Jan 27, 2027 EPS/revenue consensus (Boeing guides only FCF, deliveries and capex, not EPS/revenue)
Full 2026-2027 debt maturity schedule beyond the disclosed $4,569M current portion and the $300M Mar 2027 note
Named 13D/13G holder changes (only aggregate institutional flow data was available)

alternative_signals.claim: Boeing announced on Nov 9, 2026 it will cut ~5% of its commercial airplane workforce via layoffs and attrition (division employs nearly 50,500 of ~182,000 total), with notifications in December 2026
Deliveries: 161 in Q3 2026 (737: 124, 787: 22, 767: 10, 777: 5), 475 in the first nine months (+8.0% YoY); but October 2026 MAX deliveries of ~32 were the fewest in nearly a year
Orders keep building: 300 net orders in Q3 2026 (Turkish Airlines, Ethiopian, Lufthansa); Avolon finalized an order for 140 737-10s on Nov 4, 2026; record $745B backlog with over 6,300 airplanes

FAA progressively lifted the post-2024 38/month 737 production cap to 42 (Oct 2025) then 47 (May 2026); the new Everett North Line rolled out its first 737 MAX 10 in October 2026 but still needs FAA line certification
Labor de-risked near term: Boeing reached new contract agreements with SPEEA-represented engineers and technicians in October 2026, avoiding a strike by the ~17,000-member union
Defense wins: F/A-XX next-generation fighter selection, a seven-year PAC-3 Seeker production expansion, and a U.S. Army AH-64 Apache fleet-maintenance award; BDS backlog a record $101B
Channel checks: 737 wings are the current production constraint, engines gate 787 output, and a key supplier parts shortage is disrupting 777 freighter output expected to last through 1H 2027

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 27): revenue $24,188M (+4% YoY), GAAP loss per share ($0.26), core loss per share ($0.34), operating cash flow $1,496M, free cash flow $464M

Q3 2026 missed on earnings: core EPS -$0.34 vs about -$0.20/-$0.21 expected, though revenue of $24.19B was roughly in line to slightly above consensus (estimates cited ranged $23.84B-$23.95B); BA fell 10.75% to $168.07 on the print
Q3 free cash flow of $464M came despite approximately $0.7B of DOJ settlement payments weighing on operating cash flow
vs its own guidance: Boeing now guides 2026 737 deliveries below the ~500 target set earlier in 2026; original FY2026 guidance was $1B-$3B FCF, ~500 737 and 90-100 787 deliveries, BDS margin ~2.5%

Updated multi-year guidance given with Q3: about $2B FCF in 2026, $3B in 2027, $6B in 2028; the $10B FCF target pushed out a full year to 2029, with 2027 squeezed by ~$1B higher capex and lower customer deposits

Segment detail Q3 2026: Commercial Airplanes revenue $10,720M with operating margin (6.5)% (a $697M loss) on 161 deliveries; BDS revenue $7,935M (+15%) with 6.2% margin including a $252M HRL Laboratories sale gain; Global Services margin 18.3%; record total backlog $745B

insider_and_ownership.claim: Post-crash director buying: Chairman Steven M. Mollenkopf bought $510K (2,950 shares @ $173.03) and director Mortimer J. Buckley bought $998K (5,820 shares @ $171.55) on/about Oct 30-Nov 2, 2026, roughly doubling each stake

CEO Robert K. Ortberg's Form 4 (filed Feb 23, 2026) shows disposal of 5,016.643 shares at $236.71 via tax withholding on RSU vesting (code F) — not an open-market sale; 135,927.865 shares beneficially owned after
Officer open-market sales in February 2026: Howard McKenzie $2.46M (Feb 5 @ $233.99), Ann Schmidt $1.53M (Feb 17 @ $243.37), Uma Amuluru $351K (Feb 24 @ $233.78)
Institutional flows: net 69.3M shares sold in the latest reported quarter (-11.38% change in institutional shares held), a notable de-ownership move into the earnings miss
A Form 144 (notice of proposed sale) was filed Nov 9, 2026, alongside two Form 4s on Nov 3, 2026 — recent insider filing activity worth tracking for follow-through sales
